description.narrative:
The overarching goal of Diakonias country strategy for Colombia is to mobilise society for peacebuilding, making the conditions for peace a national priority. In particular, the organisation identifies the holistic implementation of existing peace accords, strengthened guarantees for the protection and safety of civil society organisations and the initiation of new peace-talks, as such prioritised conditions for peace.
To achieve this, Diakonia proposes to strengthen and to work together with local civil society organisations to generate significant changes and structural transformations in four interrelated areas or change processes, each with its own set of objectives and results indicators:
1. Strengthened capacity of civil society to exercise democratic participation, defence of human rights and active citizenship. 2. Implementation of the peace agreements, new peace-talks and national reconciliation. 3. Increased gender equality in social, economic and political structures. 4. Environmental justice and defence of the right to a healthy environment

Kärnstödet till Diakonia i Colombia syftar till att bidra till en stabil och varaktig fred i landet med ett nationellt, territoriellt och rättighetsbaserat perspektiv. Detta stöd är en fortsättning av en tidigare insats med ID 10781. De övergripande målen är följande:
1) Stärkt kapacitet hos det civila samhället att utöva demokratiskt deltagande, försvar av mänskliga rättigheter och aktivt medborgarskap. 2) Genomförande av fredsavtalet, nya fredssamtal och nationell försoning. 3) Ökad jämställdhet i sociala, ekonomiska och politiska strukturer. 4) Miljörättvisa och försvar av rätten till en hälsosam miljö.

The support to Diakonia cointains two components; a core funding to the country plan; and a project support to a civil society fund. The components aim at contributing to a stable and lasting peace in Colombia with a national, territorial, and right-based perspective. The overall objectives are the following:
1) Strengthened capacity of civil society to exercise democratic participation, defence of human rights and active citizenship. 2) Implementation of the peace agreement, new peace-talks, and national reconciliation. 3) Increased gender equality in social, economic, and political structures. 4) Environmental justice and defence of the right to a healthy environment.
This support is a continuation of previous contribution with ID-number 10781.

description.narrative:
The following are some of the results achieved during 2024.
CSOs were strengthened for their advocacy allowing them to participate in the construction of the National Development Plan, the formulation of 7 public policies including the Human Rights Action Plan, and the reactivation of the National Guarantee Process. The organizations have documented information about human rights violations, including 1.142 sociopolitical violence cases.
They are producing newsletters, reports, and press releases to enhance dialogue and make the human rights situation in Colombia visible. Regarding protection, more than 400 protection measures were taken to protect the lives of human rights and social leaders who were at imminent risk. Approximately 100 organizations and 300 hundred social leaders in danger have mechanisms and tools for their protection and auto protection against aggressions.
Women organizations have played an important role in the follow-up of gender measures included in the 2016 Peace Agreement and have contributed significatively in the construction of the Nacional Action Plan for the implementation of the 1325 resolution about women, peace, and security. Also, they are largely involved in the widespread and implementation of the recommendations generated by the Truth Commission.
Participation of communities and civil society on peace processes dialogues was strengthened for the presentation of inputs and proposals regarding ceasefires and humanitarian actions.
Political participation of women was strengthened. For example, in Chocó, 3 women were elected as majors of their municipalities and 37 were elected to different popular election charges. All these women participated in a training for their political empowerment.
Organizations have increased their advocacy for the protection of water and the rights to a healthy environment related to the unsustainable use of natural resources, the expansion of cattle farming and infrastructure megaprojects.
The National Human Rights Award in Colombia remains to be a strategic opportunity to make more visible the work made by social leaders and human rights defenders it also highlights their role in the strengthening of democracy. The award has big coverage in media with 130 press releases. The winners participated in advocacy visits with key political actors in the United States.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
